title: Maximum Product of Two Digits
summary: Given a positive integer n, find the highest product resulting from multiplying any two of its digits, allowing the use of the same digit more than once if present.
statement: Given a positive integer n, find the highest product resulting from multiplying any two of its digits, allowing the use of the same digit more than once if present.
constraints: Choose two digit occurrences from positive integer n.
Return the maximum product of the chosen digits.
Two equal digits may be used only when they occur in two positions.
hints: The product of the two largest nonnegative digits is maximal.
Using the final two positions respects multiplicity.
editorial: Using the final two positions respects multiplicity.

tests.explanation: The only product is three times one, equal to three.
Two occurrences of nine produce product eighty-one.
